name: BBA Custom Types
author: Amit Sharma

sections.description:
BBA Custom Types lets site owners create and manage custom post types, taxonomies, and custom field groups without editing theme files or writing registration code.

Use it when your site needs structured content beyond posts and pages: projects, testimonials, events, resources, product collections, locations, or any other content model. The plugin gives you a clear admin workflow while keeping WordPress registration keys, rewrite bases, taxonomy relationships, and postmeta fields visible and controllable.

What you can do

  • Create and manage custom post types and taxonomies from a unified dashboard.
  • Create and organize custom field groups attached to custom post types, native posts, or pages via the Field Groups submenu.
  • Support for 10 core custom field types: Text, Textarea, Number, Email, URL, Date, Select (dropdown), Radio buttons, Single Checkbox, and Checkbox Group (multi-select).
  • Configure functional field options: Defaults, Required validation, and Show in REST API exposure.
  • Seamless editing experience in both Gutenberg (Block Editor) and the Classic Editor.
  • Scoped transactional persistence under Gutenberg REST updates: ScopedTransactionCoordinator coordinates single-request REST post updates and exact-row custom field persistence with InnoDB row locking (FOR UPDATE) and automatic rollbacks on error for qualified post saves.
  • Set singular and plural labels, public URL slugs, and frontend rewrite bases for custom post types.
  • Choose supported post features, including title, editor, excerpt, featured image, author, comments, revisions, custom fields, and page attributes.
  • Configure taxonomy visibility, hierarchy, REST API support, and attached post types.
  • Receive inline validation for duplicate or invalid slugs, keys, and field options before settings are saved.
  • Drag-and-drop field reordering and collapsible field builder cards in the admin dashboard.

How it works

BBA Custom Types stores your definitions in WordPress options and registers them using core WordPress APIs. Generated internal keys such as bbact_project identify content types in the database and remain stable across edits. Public URLs can be adjusted independently with the Frontend URL base setting.

Custom fields are saved directly to native WordPress postmeta with exact-row ownership and bounded tombstones to protect historical data integrity.

The plugin is dependency-free at runtime, does not send data to external services, and does not require an account.

Getting Started

Create a custom post type

  1. Go to BBA Custom Types and select New Custom Post Type.
  2. Enter a singular name, for example Project. The plugin fills related labels for you; you can adjust any of them before saving.
  3. Review the URL slug. This is used to generate the internal key on the first save.
  4. Optionally set a different Frontend URL base. For example, leave the key based on project but use projects for public URLs.
  5. Configure public visibility, archive support, REST API support, menu position, and supported post features.
  6. Save the custom post type, then use its new menu in WordPress admin to add content.

Create a taxonomy

  1. Select New taxonomy from the BBA Custom Types dashboard.
  2. Enter a singular name, for example Project Type.
  3. Choose whether it is hierarchical. Hierarchical taxonomies behave like categories; non-hierarchical ones behave like tags.
  4. Select the custom post types that should use this taxonomy.
  5. Save the taxonomy. The new taxonomy appears with the selected post types immediately.

Create a custom field group

  1. In WordPress admin, navigate to BBA Custom Types > Field Groups (or the Field Groups submenu).
  2. Click the New Field Group button (or Create Field Group if no groups exist yet) in the toolbar to open the full-screen modal field group editor.
  3. Enter a group title and select the target post types (custom post types, Posts, or Pages).
  4. Configure group position context (Normal, Side, Advanced), priority, order, and optional instructions.
  5. In the Fields section, click + Add Field to add dynamic field rows.
  6. For each field, configure label, field key, field type (from 10 available types), placeholder, default value, required toggle, and REST API exposure. Choice-based fields (Select, Radio, Checkbox Group) include a Choices list.
  7. Click Save Field Group in the modal footer. The modal remains open with in-flight state protections, syncing the assigned group ID and revision token without full page reload.
  8. Fields render immediately in post edit screens for assigned post types.

Change a public URL base safely

Do not change the URL slug of a post type that already has content unless you intend to create a different internal post type key. Instead, change Frontend URL base to alter the public URL path while retaining the existing internal key and its posts.

After changing a rewrite base, go to Settings > Permalinks and select Save Changes once to refresh WordPress rewrite rules.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload the BBA Custom Types ZIP file and activate it.
  3. Open BBA Custom Types from the WordPress admin menu.
  4. Create a custom post type, taxonomy, or custom field group using the steps below.
sections.faq:
Does BBA Custom Types create both post types and taxonomies?

Yes. You can manage post types, taxonomies, and custom field groups from the BBA Custom Types menu.

Does the plugin include a custom field builder?

Yes! Version 1.1.0 introduces a custom field builder supporting 10 field types, field defaults, required validation, REST API exposure, and Gutenberg block editor integration.

What happens to my custom field values if I delete a field group?

Existing postmeta values stored in the database are preserved. Deleting a field group definition deletes only the schema configuration; existing row data in wp_postmeta remains intact. Durable tombstones prevent historical keys from colliding with newly registered fields.

Does the plugin support the Gutenberg block editor?

Yes. Both custom post types and custom fields integrate with Gutenberg. Custom fields feature client-side pre-save validation locks and transactional REST persistence for qualified scopes.

What is the exact scope of transactional Gutenberg persistence?

Scoped transactional persistence is coordinated by ScopedTransactionCoordinator. It currently coordinates native post updates with an applicable field group whose required validation criteria are scoped to atomic REST requests with InnoDB row locking (FOR UPDATE) and rollback protections. Other post types, multi-field groups, and Classic Editor saves use standard WordPress postmeta APIs and pre-save authorization workflows.

What is the difference between URL slug, Frontend URL base, and Internal key?

The URL slug is used when first creating a type and helps generate its internal key. The Frontend URL base controls the public permalink path. The Internal key is the WordPress identifier, for example bbact_project; it should remain unchanged after you create content.

Why did my posts disappear after changing the URL slug?

Changing the URL slug can generate a new internal key. WordPress then treats it as a new post type, so posts associated with the old key are no longer shown in the new menu. Restore the original internal key to access that content again. To change only public URLs, use Frontend URL base instead.

Can I edit the generated key?

The key is generated on first save so you can verify the intended slug before creation. Keep it stable after content exists, because WordPress uses it to associate posts, taxonomies, and metadata.

Why is my new frontend URL not working yet?

Save your permalink settings at Settings > Permalinks after changing a Frontend URL base. This refreshes WordPress rewrite rules.

Does it delete my content when I deactivate the plugin?

No. Deactivation does not delete posts, terms, metadata, or saved definitions. Registered types and fields are inactive until the plugin is reactivated.

Does the plugin use an external API or transmit site data?

No. BBA Custom Types works entirely within your WordPress installation and does not require an account or third-party service.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Feature: Added Custom Field Groups builder with support for 10 core field types (Text, Textarea, Number, Email, URL, Date, Select, Radio, Checkbox, and Checkbox Group).
  • Feature: Added functional field options: Default values, Required validation, and Show in REST API exposure.
  • Feature: Support for custom field groups on native WordPress post and page post types alongside custom post types via the Field Groups submenu.
  • Feature: Drag-and-drop field reordering and collapsible field builder cards.
  • Enhancement: Gutenberg block editor integration with client-side validation locks and pre-save authorization gates.
  • Enhancement: Scoped transactional persistence via ScopedTransactionCoordinator with InnoDB row-level locking (FOR UPDATE) and rollback safeguards for qualified REST post updates.
  • Enhancement: Durable field tombstones (MAX_TOMBSTONES = 500) to protect historical postmeta and prevent key collisions.
  • Quality: Integrated WordPress Coding Standards (WPCS) ruleset, fine-grained fingerprint regression gate, and PHPCompatibilityWP 8.0+ verification.

1.0.1

  • Added the project website link to the plugin header.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Create and manage custom post types and taxonomies from a modern WordPress admin UI.
  • Added real-time validation, editable first-save slug workflow, modal editing, and live taxonomy attachment updates.
